answer:
The energy levels for a particle in a 1D potential box of length $L$ are given by:
$$E_n = \frac{n^2 h^2}{8mL^2}$|

Given data:
- Length $L = 1\text{ \AA} = 10^{-10}\text{ m}$
- Mass of electron $m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$
- Planck's constant $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$

For the ground state ($n = 1$):
$$E_1 = \frac{1^2 \times (6.626 \times 10^{-34})^2}{8 \times (9.1 \times 10^{-31}) \times (10^{-10})^2} = 6.02 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J} = 37.6\text{ eV}$|

For $n = 2$:
$$E_2 = 2^2 \times E_1 = 4 \times 37.6\text{ eV} = 150.4\text{ eV}$|

For $n = 3$:
$$E_3 = 3^2 \times E_1 = 9 \times 37.6\text{ eV} = 338.4\text{ eV}$$
proTip: Convert the final energy values from Joules to electron-volts (eV) by dividing by $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$, as it is preferred in atomic physics.
